objective: Students will identify the main idea of an informational passage, cite at least two supporting details, draw a logical inference, and determine the meaning of a word from context.
hook: Imagine losing a leg and simply growing a brand-new one back in a few weeks.
agenda: Bell ringer (5) · Mini-lesson: main idea vs details (10) · Read + model (10) · Practice (17) · Exit (3)
assessment: The exit ticket checks whether each student can state the passage's central main idea in one clear sentence of their own words.

script.title: Bell ringer
script.do: Project the question and have students write silently, then share one answer with a partner.
options: Have students turn and talk first if the room is low-energy, then write.
script.say: In your own words, what is a 'main idea'? Write one sentence, then be ready to share.

script.title: Mini-lesson: main idea vs. details
script.do: Teach the difference using the slides; draw a table on the board with 'Main idea' on top and 'Details' as legs holding it up.
options: Use a physical prop: a tabletop resting on four 'detail' legs to show support.
script.say: The main idea is the point the whole passage is making; details are the smaller facts that hold it up like table legs.

script.title: Read + model
script.do: Read the axolotl passage aloud while students follow along, then think aloud to find the main idea and underline two supporting details.
options: Do a shared choral read of the first three sentences, then continue solo.
script.say: Watch how I ask, 'What is this whole passage mostly about?' before I decide on the main idea.

script.title: Practice
script.do: Students complete the worksheet independently, then check with a partner; circulate and coach students who confuse a detail with the main idea.
options: Allow partners to answer the first question together, then finish the rest alone.
script.say: Remember: a detail is true, but the main idea covers the whole passage. Answer in complete sentences.

script.title: Exit
script.do: Collect the exit ticket as students leave and scan for any who restated a single detail instead of the main idea.
options: Have students read their sentence to a partner before turning it in.
script.say: In one sentence, tell me the main idea of today's passage.

slides.heading: Grow a new leg?
bullets: One animal can regrow a lost leg in weeks
It can even repair its own heart and brain
Today we find the MAIN IDEA of its story

slides.heading: Main idea vs. details
bullets: main idea = the point the whole passage makes
details = the facts, examples, and reasons that support it
how to find the main idea: ask 'What is this MOSTLY about?' and look at the title, first, and last sentences

slides.heading: Model
bullets: Ask: what is the WHOLE passage about?
Underline facts that repeat the same point
Turn that point into one sentence
slides.example: In a short paragraph about how bees help farms by pollinating crops, spreading pollen, and boosting harvests, the details all point to one main idea: bees are important because they help farmers grow food.

slides.heading: You try
bullets: Read the axolotl passage on your worksheet
Ask yourself: what is this MOSTLY about?
Underline two details that support your answer

notes:
## Main Idea & Details
**Main idea:** The single most important point the whole passage is making. Ask, 'What is this MOSTLY about?'
**Details:** The facts, examples, and reasons that support and prove the main idea. They answer who, what, when, where, why, and how.
**Strategy:** Check the title, first sentence, and last sentence; notice ideas that repeat; then state the main idea in one sentence of your own words. Watch out: a single true fact is usually a detail, not the main idea.

worksheet.title: Main Idea & Supporting Details: The Amazing Axolotl
worksheet.instructions:
Read the passage, then answer.

Read: The axolotl is a small salamander that never fully grows up. Most amphibians change form as they age, but the axolotl keeps its feathery gills and stays in the water its entire life. Scientists call this staying young forever a trait called neoteny. What amazes researchers most is the axolotl's power to heal. If it loses a leg, it can grow a brand-new one, complete with bone, muscle, and nerves, in just a few weeks. It can even repair parts of its heart and brain without leaving a scar. Because of this rare ability, laboratories around the world study the axolotl, hoping to unlock secrets that could someday help human patients heal serious injuries. Sadly, in the wild this remarkable creature is nearly extinct, surviving in only a few canals near Mexico City.

problems: What is the main idea of the passage?
Give 2 details that support the main idea (list two).
The passage says laboratories around the world study the axolotl. Based on the passage, why do scientists think this animal is worth studying?
What does the word 'neoteny' mean as it is used in this passage?

answers: The main idea is that the axolotl is a remarkable salamander whose rare ability to stay young and heal itself makes it valuable to scientists, even though it is nearly extinct in the wild.

Two supporting details are: (1) if it loses a leg, it can grow a brand-new one with bone, muscle, and nerves in just a few weeks; and (2) it can even repair parts of its heart and brain without leaving a scar.
Scientists think the axolotl is worth studying because its rare healing ability might help them unlock secrets that could someday help human patients heal serious injuries.
In this passage, 'neoteny' means the trait of staying young forever, or keeping young features like feathery gills and living in the water for its whole life instead of changing form as it ages.

exitTicket: In one sentence, what was the main idea of today's passage?
